newsitem.title: INDIA: India 14-day t-bill seen helping term money market.
newsitem.headline: India 14-day t-bill seen helping term money market.

text.p: The Reserve Bank of India's (RBI) maiden auction of 14-day day treasury bills on Friday will give a further impetus to evolution of a term money market, dealers said.
The RBI had set the floor for evolution of a term money market when it scrapped cash reserve requirement on inter-bank borrowings in its April 15 credit and monetary policy.
The auction, results of which are due around 1730 local (1200 GMT), will also bring stability to the overnight call market, bankers said.
"Once it (14-day treasury bill) is stabilised, call should not touch a low of 0.25 percent," Babu Raghutham, chief manager (treasury) at Global Trust Bank Ltd said.
"Call should find a support level of 5.0 percent," he said.
Most dealers expect the RBI to discontinue its current three- and four-day repo auctions once 14-day bills take off.
"The RBI can't have two competing instruments for controlling liquidity," a dealer said.
"Some banks are apprehensive about the cut-off (rate at Friday's auction)," said a primary dealer. "If it is kept low and should call rates rise next week, people will lose money."
Many dealers expect a yield of 4.5-5.0 at the auction.
RBI said it planned treasury bills of various maturities. Friday's 14-day auction is expected to be followed up by treasury bills of other maturities in the near future.
Some bankers said the new bill will deepen the market and help companies wanting to park short-term funds.
"Corporates now buying 91-day t-bills two weeks before maturity can now shift to the 14-day bill," said a dealer.
